summary: Iter13 verified: (1) FRONTEND_TEST_MSG completely eliminated — 0 rows in messages collection, settings.global.inactivity_auto_message and welcome_message are both None (fall back to DEFAULT_AUTO_MSG 'Thanks for waiting…'). (2) Email capture UI is fully removed from ChatWidget — no email-capture/email-inline* testids or phrases in initial Lily view or after picking a Lily option (queued/chat view); no lucide-mail icons rendered. (3) Quick Replies CRUD works end-to-end (admin create → agent list → admin delete). (4) File upload/download works both directions (customer→agent with ?auth=<token>, agent→customer with session_id+session_token). Backend 7/7 pass, 1 skipped (admin/sessions probing was best-effort).
critical_code_review_comments: ChatWidget.jsx is still ~953 lines — exceeds 700-line guideline; consider extracting AttachmentBubble, LilyStage, and CSAT sub-components.
AgentDashboard.jsx also >900 lines (see iter12 review) — split recommended.

quick_replies.py has no role guard — any authenticated user (including agent) can POST/DELETE. Consider restricting create/delete to admin only if that's the intended policy (spec says 'as admin, create'; the agent could technically create/delete too). Low priority.
Anonymous file upload endpoint accepts session_id+session_token as multipart form data — verify rate limiting is applied to prevent abuse (out of scope for this iter).
seed_data_creation: Test creates anon sessions with client_id prefix 'iter13_' and one quick reply titled 'TEST_iter13_QR' which is deleted at the end of the test. No residual data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Customer→backend messaging is via WebSocket (not REST /messages route — returns 405). Use ws://.../api/ws/session/{sid}?token=... for e2e message tests. Backend accepts REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL from env — pytest run needs it exported (frontend/.env is the source of truth). settings/global doc currently has welcome_message=None and inactivity_auto_message=None which is correct (scheduler falls back to DEFAULT_AUTO_MSG constant).
